Reconstruct the complete mathematical chain for Internal Energy, Heat, and Work, from the starting relation to the final result. Include every required substitution, derivative, integral, or limiting step.
Start:
\[
\Delta U=U_f-U_i=\int_i^f dU.
\tag*{[1]}
\]

Target:
\[
dU=\delta Q-\delta W,
\qquad
\Delta U=Q-W.
\tag*{[4]}
\]
Notation: \(U,U_i,U_f\) denotes internal energy and its initial and final values; unit \(\mathrm{J}\); \(dU\) denotes exact infinitesimal change in internal energy; unit \(\mathrm{J}\); \(\Delta U=U_f-U_i\) denotes finite change in internal energy; unit \(\mathrm{J}\); \(\delta Q,Q\) denotes inexact infinitesimal heat transfer and finite heat transferred into the system; unit \(\mathrm{J}\); \(\delta W,W\) denotes inexact infinitesimal work transfer and finite work done by the system; unit \(\mathrm{J}\).
questions.answer:
Model:
Internal energy belongs to the state of a system, whereas heat and work describe energy crossing the system boundary during a process. A system does not contain heat or work. With the Academy convention, heat into the system is positive and work done by the system is positive.

A positive \(Q\) raises the system's energy if nothing else changes. A positive \(W\) removes energy from the system because the system supplies that work to its surroundings.

Working:
Step 1:
\[
\Delta U=U_f-U_i=\int_i^f dU.
\tag*{[1]}
\]

Consequently, the internal-energy change around any closed cycle vanishes:

Step 2:
\[
\oint dU=0.
\tag*{[2]}
\]

Heat and work are transfers, not state functions. Their process totals are path integrals,

Step 3:
\[
Q=\int_i^f\delta Q,
\qquad
W=\int_i^f\delta W,
\tag*{[3]}
\]

so two paths between the same states can have different values of \(Q\) and \(W\). The inexact symbol \(\delta\) is therefore essential; ordinary exact-differential notation must not be used for these path transfers.

Energy conservation connects the exact state change to the two inexact transfers:

Step 4:
\[
dU=\delta Q-\delta W,
\qquad
\Delta U=Q-W.
\tag*{[4]}
\]

Final answer:
\[
dU=\delta Q-\delta W,
\qquad
\Delta U=Q-W.
\tag*{[4]}
\]

Check:
Each step uses the same definitions and constraints, and adjacent equations are dimensionally consistent.
